title: In 2 Kings 18 What Does The Response Of God To Hezekiahs Prayer Teach Us About Divine Intervention In Our Lives
paragraphs: Hezekiah’s Prayer and God’s Response: A Study in Divine Intervention (2 Kings 18–19)

The reign of King Hezekiah stands out in the biblical narrative as a remarkable period marked by faithfulness to God amid intense external pressure. In 2 Kings 18, we see Hezekiah facing a dire threat from the Assyrian empire, the superpower of the day. The way Hezekiah seeks the Lord and the Lord’s response offers profound insights into divine intervention in the lives of believers.
Background: The Crisis at Jerusalem
Hezekiah becomes king and institutes reforms, removing idols and restoring true worship (2 Kings 18:4). His faithfulness is summarized:
He trusted in Jehovah, the God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among them that were before him. - 2 Kings 18:5 ASV

However, the Assyrian king Sennacherib invades Judah, besieging Jerusalem. Hezekiah faces a situation beyond his own power to resolve. Sennacherib’s messengers mock God, urging the people not to trust in Him (2 Kings 18:29-35).
Hezekiah’s Response: Turning to God in Prayer

In the midst of this crisis, Hezekiah’s response is instructive. Instead of relying on alliances or panicking, he first seeks the Lord in humble prayer (2 Kings 19:1). He takes the Assyrian threats and "spread it before Jehovah" (2 Kings 19:14), recognizing his own helplessness and God’s sovereignty.
Now, O Jehovah our God, save thou us, I beseech thee, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Jehovah God, even thou only. - 2 Kings 19:19 ASV
Hezekiah’s prayer is not just for personal deliverance, but that God’s name would be glorified among the nations.
God’s Response: The Power and Purpose of Divine Intervention
God responds through the prophet Isaiah, assuring Hezekiah that He has heard his prayer:
Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard thee. - 2 Kings 19:20 ASV

God promises deliverance, declaring that Sennacherib will not enter the city nor shoot an arrow there (2 Kings 19:32). That very night, the angel of the Lord strikes down 185,000 Assyrian soldiers, and Sennacherib withdraws in defeat (2 Kings 19:35).
Key Insights for Our Lives

Divine Intervention Begins with Humble Prayer: Hezekiah’s example teaches us that God delights to intervene when His people humbly seek Him, acknowledging their dependence. See also Philippians 4:6 and James 5:16.
God Acts for His Glory: Hezekiah prays that God’s name would be exalted. God’s interventions are often aimed at displaying His power and faithfulness, not just meeting our needs (Psalm 115:1).
God’s Sovereignty is Supreme: The Lord controls the hearts of kings and the fate of nations. Nothing is too hard for Him (Jeremiah 32:17).

Faith Does Not Eliminate Trouble, But Brings God’s Presence Into It: Despite Hezekiah’s faithfulness, the threat came. God’s people are not promised freedom from trials, but are promised His presence and intervention according to His perfect wisdom (Isaiah 43:2).

God’s Answers Can Be Immediate or Delayed: In this case, God answered dramatically and quickly. At other times, His intervention may not be as immediate, but He always hears the prayers of His people (Psalm 34:17).
The Christ-Centered Perspective

As with all of Scripture, this account points forward to Christ. Hezekiah’s intercession and God’s deliverance foreshadow the ultimate deliverance God provides through Jesus. The greatest intervention in history is God sending His Son to rescue us from sin and death (John 3:16). Our access to God’s throne in prayer is secured by Christ’s sacrifice (Hebrews 4:16).
Conclusion

Hezekiah’s story encourages believers to bring their fears and crises to God, trusting that He hears, cares, and acts for His glory and our good. Divine intervention may look different in each situation, but God is always faithful to His promises and attentive to the prayers of His people.
